row.team_price_text: Contact Sales (MDR priced on users, servers and internet egress points)
row.evidence: Arctic Wolf's Unified Portal supports OIDC federated authentication, while contacts (portal users) are added in Organization Profile > Contacts and removed by a ticket fulfilled by the Concierge Security Team; no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New row. Arctic Wolf sells MDR and related services on quote, sized by users, servers and internet egress points, so price fields are null (Managed Security Awareness is sold separately from $2.99 per user/mo). Portal SSO is OIDC federation set up by a primary or secondary contact in Organization Profile > Federated Authentication, with guides for Azure, Duo, Google Workspace, Okta and OneLogin as custom OIDC apps; no edition gate is stated. Portal users (contacts) are added manually, the first by the Concierge Security Team, and deletion is a ticket the CST fulfils (access is removed at once). The only documented user API is the Aurora Endpoint Defense (ex-Cylance) console User API at protectapi.cylance.com/users/v2 (JWT with user:* scopes); there is no Unified Portal user API. Okta OIN search finds no Arctic Wolf app. 'None' is by absence (rule 5).

rate_limits.text: 100,000 requests per day, or about 10 requests per second, depending on the service endpoint; 429 on excess.

limitations.text: The Aurora User API does not support custom roles.

user_api.notes: Applies to the Aurora Endpoint Defense console only, not the Arctic Wolf Unified Portal (MDR), whose contacts are managed in the UI. Personal API keys exist in the Unified Portal for third-party integrations, but no portal user endpoints are documented.

okta.notes: OIN search returned no Arctic Wolf app; Arctic Wolf's Okta guide has customers create a custom OIDC app integration.

entra.notes: learn.microsoft.com arctic-wolf-tutorial returns 404; Arctic Wolf documents Azure as a custom OIDC federation.

google.notes: Arctic Wolf has a Google Workspace federation guide (custom OIDC); no Marketplace app checked.

onelogin.notes: Arctic Wolf has a OneLogin federation guide (custom OIDC); connector page not checked.

fallbacks.notes: Docs do not say whether a federated sign-in by an unknown user creates a contact; contacts are otherwise added manually.

citations.title: FAQ - Managed Detection and Response | Arctic Wolf
citations.quote: The MDR approach is to provide coverage across your attack surface based on number of users, servers, and internet egress points

citations.title: Federated Authentication | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Federated authentication allows you to use your preferred OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider (IdP) to authenticate with Arctic Wolf® web portals.

citations.title: Generic Federated Authentication Configuration | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Configure the IdP sign-in method as OpenID Connect. The redirect or reply URI for Arctic Wolf is https://auth.arcticwolf.com/login/callback.

citations.title: Okta | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Sign-in method — Select OIDC - OpenID Connect.

citations.title: Add a Contact | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Your Concierge Security® Team (CST) must add the first contact with the email domain that your organization uses. After your CST adds the first contact, you can add other contacts with the same email domain.

citations.title: Add a Contact | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Only Primary and Secondary contacts can view and manage the Contacts page in the Unified Portal.

citations.title: Remove a Contact | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: The system creates a ticket with your request to delete the contact. This contact remains listed until your Concierge Security® Team (CST) fulfills your request, but the system automatically edits this contact to remove access to Arctic Wolf® services.

citations.title: User API | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: User access to the Aurora Endpoint Security console and what they can view depends on their permissions. The User API does not support custom roles

citations.title: Create user | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Create a new console user. This requires a unique email address for the user being created.

citations.title: Create user | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Authorization: Bearer JWT Token returned by Auth API with the user:create encoded.

citations.title: Get users | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: The maximum page size that can be specified is 200 entries per page.

citations.title: Get user | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Request information for a specific console user resource belonging to a tenant.

citations.title: Update user | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Update an existing console user resource.

citations.title: Delete user | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Delete an existing console user resource.

citations.title: Send invite email | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: Request the console login invitation email to be resent to a user who has not logged into the console yet.

citations.title: API and management console rate limit | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: The rate limiting for API endpoints and the management console is 100,000 requests per day, or about 10 requests per second, depending on the service endpoint.

citations.title: Contacts | Arctic Wolf Help Documentation
citations.quote: On the Arctic Wolf® Unified Portal Contacts page, you can manage the administration and security permissions of contacts in your organization who interact with Arctic Wolf.
